description: I'm a school student passionate about space, science, and technology. For NASA Space Apps' “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge, I want to use NASA data, research, and creative storytelling to explore abandoned equipment and uncover the stories behind them. I'm eager to collaborate, think creatively, and build a meaningful project. Skills in research, coding, data analysis, and design are welcome!
summary:
"Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" is an emotional short film and interactive web archive honoring NASA’s discarded hardware on the Moon and Mars. 

To address the challenge, I created a narrated short film paired with a custom-coded website featuring real NASA imagery, archival mission footage, and exact landing coordinates. The story spotlights three iconic pioneers: the Apollo 16 Lunar Roving Vehicle resting beside a family photograph on the Moon since 1972; the Perseverance Sky Crane that deliberately flew away to crash after safely delivering its rover; and the Opportunity rover ("Oppy"), which survived nearly 15 years before sending its final message during a global dust storm.

This project is important because it transforms technical mission data into a human story. By remembering the quiet sacrifices of these machines—and studying how they endure decades in space—we inspire future generations to keep innovating and exploring the unknown.
details:
• What Does It Do & How Does It Work? A multimedia project featuring a narrated short film and interactive web archive that explores three stranded extraterrestrial vehicles using NASA coordinates and mission data:
    • Apollo 16 LRV-2: Located at the Descartes Highlands (8.9730° S, 15.5002° E) with Charles Duke's family photograph.
    • Perseverance Sky Crane: Located at Jezero Crater (18.38° N, 77.58° E), engineered to crash-land safely away from the rover.
    • Opportunity Rover ("Oppy"): Located in Perseverance Valley (1.95° S, 354.47° E), which operated for nearly 15 years before its historic final message.
  • Benefits & Intended Impact: Transforms technical space history into an emotional narrative to inspire the public while gathering insights on how hardware withstands cosmic radiation and harsh planetary environments for future Artemis and Mars missions.
  • Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used: Built with HTML5 and CSS3 deployed on Netlify, video produced via Canva using NASA archival assets, and AI text-to-speech utilized in compliance with NASA Space Apps privacy guidelines.
  • Creativity & Key Factors Considered: Combines emotional storytelling and accurate NASA/JPL/HiRISE mission data with strict youth accessibility and privacy standards.
